ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Section III invites Jews and Quraysh to the Qur’an's natural straight path, contrasts the fates of acceptance and rejection, rebukes those blind to signs who demand punishment, and alludes to God's practice of punishing nations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: both the Jews and the Idolaters of the Quraysh are invited to profess faith in the Qur’ ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: At Judgment no soul bears another's burden; each person sees and carries the burden of their own deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Every person will observe his deeds and carry their burden alone

BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r1.claim: Read your book is an indirect command, meaning it will be said to the person to read.
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r1.anchor: على إرادة القول أي : يقال إقرأ كتابك

BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r2.claim: Qatada says the person reads it even if he could not read in worldly life.
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة يقرأ ذلك يوم من لم يكن في الدنيا قارئا

BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r3.claim: The grammar treats ba as extra, al-yawm as the adverb, hasiban as the specification, and alayka as governed by the sense of accountant; the masculine form interprets nafs as a person.
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r3.anchor: أي : كفى نفسك والباء زائدة واليوم ظرف

BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r4.claim: God leaves each servant to account for himself so God cannot be accused of injustice and the proof is established through the servant's own confession.
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r4.anchor: وفوض تعالى حساب العبد إليه لئلا ينسب إلى الظلم ولتجب الحجة عليه باعترافه

BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan calls it fair that God makes a person account for himself.
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r5.anchor: قال الحسن : انصف من انصفك أنصف من جعلك حسيب نفسك

BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r6.speaker: عمر
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r6.claim: Umar urges people to take stock before judgment, review their deeds while they can still make amends, and remember that tomorrow offers no chance to repair them.
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r6.anchor: عمر رضي الله عنه كفته كه حاسبوا قبل أن تحاسبوا امروز دفتر اعمال

BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r7.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r7.claim: A report in Kashf al-Asrar has a king ask his self each evening to recount the day's words, deeds, movements, and stillness; the self begs to be released from the burden, because it cannot endure even a day's accounting.
BURSEVI:v5p107#2/r7.anchor: دركشف الاسرار آورده كه درى سر خويش را كفت امروز هره بامردم كويى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r1.claim: “Read your book” is what the person is told; the clause may be an adjective, circumstantial clause, or independent statement.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r1.anchor: بتقدير يقال له ذلك وهذه الجملة إما صفة أو حال أو مستأنفة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r2.claim: In “yourself suffices,” the mainstream parses “yourself” as the subject with an added bāʾ; the address yāʾ is a separation marker, sometimes omitted in poetry.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r2.anchor: وكفى فعل ماض وبنفسك فاعله والياء سيف خطيب وجاء إسقاطها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r3.speaker: الشاعر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r3.claim: Two poetic examples use “كَفى” to show the construction, including a line where gray hair and Islam suffice as an admonition.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r4.claim: Grammarians note the verb lacks feminine agreement with “nafs”; although agreement can vary for a nonhuman feminine subject after an added preposition, analogous verbs do show it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r4.anchor: ولم تلحق الفعل علامة التأنيث وإن كان مثله تلحقه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r5.claim: Some instead make the subject “sufficiency” or treat kafā as an imperative-like particle with an implicit addressee, so the bāʾ is not extra; the majority prefers the earlier parse.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r5.anchor: ومن هنا قيل إن فاعل كفى ضمير يعود على الاكتفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r6.claim: “Today” is a time adverb; ḥasīban is either specification or circumstantial, and “against you” fits the sense of an accountant who counts a person’s acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r6.anchor: ( اليوم ) ظرف لكفى و ( حسيبا ) تمييز

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r7.claim: Ḥasīb may mean accountant or sufficient witness; describing the feminine nafs with masculine ḥasīb is explained by the male-associated role, by treating nafs as person, or by the adjective’s pattern.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#3/r7.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالنفس الذات فكأنه قيل كفى بك حسيبا عليك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r1.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r1.claim: Muqatil takes “yourself” to mean the bodily limbs that testify against a person when he denies his deeds; the author calls this contrary to the apparent meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r1.anchor: وعن مقاتل أن المراد بالنفس الجوارح فإنها تشهد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r2.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r2.claim: When reciting the verse, al-Hasan says God has dealt fairly with a person by making him the judge of himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r2.anchor: وعن الحسن أنه كان إذا قرأ الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r3.claim: The command applies to believers and unbelievers; al-Suddi’s account of an unbeliever asking to judge himself does not restrict the verse to unbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r3.anchor: والظاهر أنه يقال ذلك للمؤمن والكافر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r4.claim: Qatada reports that on Judgment Day even one who could not read in worldly life will read the record.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r4.anchor: ويقرأ في ذلك اليوم كما روي عن قتادة من لم يكن قارئا في الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r5.claim: A report describes the believer first seeing sins in the record, fearing ruin, then finding them forgiven and reading good deeds with growing joy and light.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r5.anchor: وجاء أن المؤمن يقرأ أولا سيآته وحسناته في ظهر كتابه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r6.claim: The corresponding account says an unbeliever sees good deeds rejected, is darkened with grief, and then reads his sins; the report cites the rejected deeds and his lament over the book.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r6.anchor: وأما الكافر فيقرأ أولا حسناته وسيآته في ظهر كتابه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r7.claim: A mystical-philosophical interpretation identifies the book with the soul bearing hidden imprints of deeds, revealed after bodily separation; the author says this is remote from the plain sense and treats resurrection as a lesser resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r7.anchor: وفسر بعضهم الكتاب بالنفس المتنفسة بآثار الأعمال ونشره وقراءته بظهور ذلك له ولغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r8.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r8.claim: The Imam says the narrated outward events are true and the verse can also bear spiritual meanings, so one should affirm both; Khafaji says this need not contradict transmitted reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r8.anchor: إن الحق أن الأحوال الظاهرة التي وردت فيها الروايات حق وصدق لا مرية فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r9.claim: The author doubts that the spiritual reading is an apparent meaning or that Qatada’s statement supports it; reading the illiterate person’s record literally is itself an alternative interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p33/r9.anchor: ولعل قتادة وأمثاله من سلف الأمة لا يخطر لهم أمثال هذه التأويلات ببال

ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r1.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r1.claim: The Imam’s first coherence link is that the Qur’an has supplied needed proofs of divine oneness, prophethood, and resurrection, leaving no excuse when people face judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r1.anchor: كل ما يحتاج إليه من دلائل التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد قد صار مذكورا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r2.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r2.claim: Second, God’s many religious and worldly benefits require service and obedience, so each person is questioned about words and deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r2.anchor: أوصل إلى الخلق أصناف الأشياء النافعة لهم في الدين والدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r3.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r3.claim: Third, since God created humans to worship and made material things useful for them, judgment asks whether each person obeyed or rebelled.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r3.anchor: وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون

ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r4.claim: The author offers another link: the preceding passage describes God’s book of guidance, while this one describes the human record that omits no small or great deed; a person’s record reflects whether he followed that first book.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p34/r4.anchor: إن فيما تقدم شرح حال كتاب الله تعالى المتضمن بيان النافع والضار من الأعمال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r6.claim: Hasan says it is just that a person must account for themselves; “reckoner” means one who accounts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r6.anchor: {كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا} محاسبا. قال الحسن: لقد عدل عليك من جعلك حسيب نفسك.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r7.claim: Qatada says even those who could not read in life will read their record then.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r7.anchor: قال قتادة: سيقرأ يومئذ من لم يكن قارئا في الدنيا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:14/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:14/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:14/r1.claim: “Read your book” assumes an omitted verb of saying.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:14/r1.anchor: اقرأ كتبك } على إرادة القول. { كفى بنفسك

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:14/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:14/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:14/r2.claim: A person suffices as his own judge today: the bā in “by yourself” is extra, and “accountant” is a specification; the word means reckoner or one who suffices, hence witness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:14/r2.anchor: أي كفى نفسك، والباء مزيدة و { حسيبا } تمييز

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:14/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:14/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:14/r3.claim: The masculine form reflects the usual male roles of accounting and testimony, or treats the soul as a person.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:14/r3.anchor: وتذكيره على أن الحساب والشهادة مما يتولاه الرجال

BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r5.claim: The person reads the book personally rather than relying on another reader; God grants this ability whether the person is literate or not.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r5.anchor: أنت بنفسك غير ملزم بما يقرأه غيرك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r6.claim: The record has no additions or omissions; if the tongue denies an entry, the person's limbs testify against it.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r6.anchor: ولا ترى فيه زيادة ولا نقصا , ولا تقدر أن تنكر منه حرفا

DURR-FULL:v5p250/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r1.claim: After the unbeliever asks to judge himself, he is told to read his book, which suffices as his reckoner.
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r1.anchor: فيقال له: {اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا}

DURR-FULL:v5p250/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r4.claim: Even a person who could not read in worldly life will read on that day.
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {اقرأ كتابك} قال: سيقرأ يومئذ من لم يكن قارئا في الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v5p250/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r5.claim: Two noble angels write each person's record; at death it is rolled and placed around the person's neck in the grave until resurrection, when the person reads it.
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r5.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: يا ابن آدم بسطت لك صحيفة ووكل بك ملكان كريمان أحدهما عن يمينك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r1.claim: After encouragement and warning, the passage highlights God’s exhaustive knowledge of deeds, comparing their precise accounting to written records; the specific human deeds follow the general “everything” for emphasis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r1.anchor: فأعقب ذكر ما فصله الله من الأشياء بالتنبيه على تفصيل أعمال الناس تفصيلا لا يقبل الشك ولا الإخفاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r3.claim: “Read your book” is direct speech whose omitted speaker is clear from the context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r3.anchor: مقول قول محذوف دل عليه السياق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r4.claim: The imperative is a compelled challenge that removes their excuse and establishes proof; the person already knows the deeds recorded.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r4.anchor: والأمر في { اقرأ } مستعمل في التسخير ومكنى به عن الإعذار لهم والاحتجاج عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r5.claim: Reading here means knowing one’s recorded deeds, or understanding miraculous inscriptions if the book has written marks.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r5.anchor: مستعملة في معرفة ما أثبت للإنسان من الأعمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r6.claim: The bā’ in بنفسك is an added emphatic marker before the subject of كفى, as in the Quranic “God suffices as witness.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r6.anchor: مزيدة للتأكيد داخلة على فاعل { كفى } كما تقدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r7.claim: Ḥasīban is an accusative specification meaning “reckoner”; عَلَيْكَ implies bearing witness, and the referent is the person from the preceding verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r7.anchor: أي من جهة حسيب . والحسيب : فعيل بمعنى فاعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r10.claim: “Read your book” uses concise ellipsis; ḥasīban means accountant and is accusative of specification.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r10.anchor: وقوله اقرأ كتابك حذف من الكلام يقال له اختصار الدلالة الظاهرة عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p443/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p443/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p443/r2.claim: Qatāda says even those unable to read in life will read their books at resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p443/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله: اقرأ كتابك إنه سيقرأ يومئذ من لم يكن يقرأ

SULAMI:v1p384#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p384#3/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
SULAMI:v1p384#3/r1.claim: Umar urges people to judge themselves before judgment, weigh deeds before they are weighed, and prepare for the greatest presentation before appearing.
SULAMI:v1p384#3/r1.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه : حاسبوا أنفسكم قبل أن تحاسبوا وزنوا أعمالكم قبل أن توزنوا

SULAMI:v1p384#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p384#3/r2.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v1p384#3/r2.claim: Yahya ibn Muadh explains that people should read their book because they themselves dictated it.
SULAMI:v1p384#3/r2.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ : اقرأ كتابك : فإنك كنت المملي له

SULAMI:v1p384#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p384#3/r3.speaker: بعض السلف
SULAMI:v1p384#3/r3.claim: An early authority says God did well to make each person their own accountant.
SULAMI:v1p384#3/r3.anchor: قال بعض السلف : لقد أحسن الله إليك من خلقك حسيب بنفسك

SULAMI:v1p384#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p384#3/r4.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p384#3/r4.claim: A saying contrasts the righteous, who are reckoned in this world, with the wicked, whose reckoning comes in the afterlife.
SULAMI:v1p384#3/r4.anchor: وقيل : محاسبة الأبرار في الدنيا ، ومحاسبة الفجار في الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r1.claim: He reads iqraʾ with a light hamza; the construction omits the understood phrase, meaning the person is told to read the book.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر اقرأ بتخفيف الهمزة وفيه اضمار تقديره فيقال له اقرأ كتابك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r2.claim: Everyone will read the record, whether or not they were literate in life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r2.anchor: قال الحسن يقرؤه أميا كان أو غير أمي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r3.claim: The one who made a person account for himself has dealt justly with him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r3.anchor: ولقد عدل عليك من جعلك حسيب نفسك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r4.claim: Ḥasīb has three interpretations: one who reckons, a witness, or one who suffices.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r4.anchor: وفي معنى حسيبا ثلاثة اقوال احدها محاسبا والثاني شاهدا والثالث كافيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r5.claim: Self-accounting lets a person see God's justice, the proof against them, and why punishment is deserved; entry to Paradise is by God's grace, while entry to Hell is because of one's own sin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r5.anchor: ليعلم عدل الله بين العباد ويرى وجوب حجة الله عليه واستحقاقه العقوبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r6.claim: The masculine ḥasīban with feminine nafs is explained by meaning the person, or because nafs has no visible feminine marker and resembles nouns such as sky and earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r6.anchor: وانما قال حسيبا والنفس مؤنثة لأنه يعني بالنفس الشخص أو لأنه لا علامة للتأنيث في لفظ النفس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p16/r7.claim: Arabic poetry likewise uses a masculine predicate with earth, cited as a parallel to the grammatical construction.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r5.claim: The person can serve as his own accountant because he knows he was not wronged and remembers what he did; nothing but his own deeds was recorded against him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r5.anchor: أي: إنك (3) تعلم أنك لم تظلم ولم يكتب عليك غير ما عملت؛ لأنك ذكرت جميع ما كان منك

TUSTARI:17:14/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:17:14/r1.speaker: الحسن البصري
TUSTARI:17:14/r1.claim: Hasan urges people to prepare a reply for the questioning and make it sound, or prepare a shroud for the Fire.
TUSTARI:17:14/r1.anchor: قال: حكي عن الحسن البصري أنه قال: أعد للسؤال جوابا وللجواب صوابا، وإلا فأعد للنار جلبابا.

TUSTARI:17:14/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:17:14/r2.speaker: عمر
TUSTARI:17:14/r2.claim: Umar says to audit and weigh yourselves before you are audited and weighed, and prepare for the great presentation before it comes.
TUSTARI:17:14/r2.anchor: وقال عمر رضي الله عنه: حاسبوا أنفسكم قبل أن تحاسبوا وزنوا أنفسكم قبل أن توزنوا وتأهبوا للعرض الأكبر

TUSTARI:17:14/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:17:14/r3.speaker: سهل
TUSTARI:17:14/r3.claim: Self-accounting is either private, between servant and God, or public, between the person and other people.
TUSTARI:17:14/r3.anchor: فسئل سهل عن المحاسبة والموازنة، فقال: المحاسبة على وجهين: محاسبة فيما بين العبد وربه، وهو سر، ومحاسبة فيما بينه وبين الخلق وهي علانية،

TUSTARI:17:14/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:17:14/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:17:14/r4.claim: When choosing between two duties, sunnas, or voluntary acts, begin with whichever is nearer to God and weightier with Him.
TUSTARI:17:14/r4.anchor: والموازنة إذا استقبلك فرضان أو سنتان أو نافلتان نظرت أيهما أقرب إلى الله وأوزن عنده، فابتدأت به.

JISHUMI:v6p4173/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r4.claim: Reading one's record removes excuses, completes the proof, and shows that God wrongs no one.
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r4.anchor: ويدل قوله: (كفى بنفسك) على قطع العذر، وتمام الحجة،

JISHUMI:v6p4173/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r5.claim: The verse establishes reckoning and records in the afterlife.
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r5.anchor: وتدل على إثبات المحاسبة والصحف في الآخرة.

JISHUMI:v6p4173/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r16.claim: If God creates the act of reading, the command to read would have no meaningful function.
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r16.anchor: ومنها: قوله: اقرأ فإن كانت القراءة خلقا له لما كان لقوله: اقرأ معنى.

JISHUMI:v6p4174/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4174/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4174/r1.claim: Calling the person an accountant makes that person accountable; under determinism, God would instead be accountable for the deed.
JISHUMI:v6p4174/r1.anchor: ومنها: قوله: حسيبا ولو كان هو الخالق لكان عليه حسابه

JISHUMI:v6p4174/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4174/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4174/r2.claim: God's accounting displays that people are repaid without injustice; creating disbelief and preventing faith would make it pointless and unjust.
JISHUMI:v6p4174/r2.anchor: ومنها: أنه يحاسب ليظهر لأهل الجمع أنه مجازى بعمله ولا يظلمه،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r6.claim: The command read assumes an unspoken we say; Qatada says even someone who could not read in life will read the record that day.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r6.anchor: اقرأ } على إرادة القول . وعن قتادة : يقرأ ذلك اليوم من لم يكن في الدنيا قارئا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r7.claim: Bi-nafsika is the subject of suffices; ḥasīban is an accusative of specification meaning accountant, by analogy to other occupational forms.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r7.anchor: و { بنفسك } فاعل كفى . { حسيبا } تمييز وهو بمعنى حاسب كضريب القداح بمعنى ضاربها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r8.claim: Alternatively, ḥasīb means sufficient as a witness and governs the preposition ʿalā; a witness suffices a claimant in what concerns him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى الكافي وضع موضع الشهيد فعدي بعلى لأن الشاهد يكفي المدعي ما أهمه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r9.claim: The masculine form evokes roles usually held by men, or nafs can mean a person irrespective of grammatical gender.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r9.anchor: قلت : لأنه بمنزلة الشهيد والقاضي والأمير ؛ لأن الغالب أن هذه الأمور يتولاها الرجال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r10.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r10.claim: When al-Hasan recited the verse he said God has dealt fairly by making each person his own judge.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r10.anchor: وكان الحسن إذا قرأها قال : يا ابن آدم ، أنصفك والله من جعلك حسيب نفسك

FARRA:v2p117/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p117/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p117/r9.claim: اقرأ كتابك has an omitted passive expression, “it will be said”; he compares other Qur’anic clauses with omitted introductory speech.
FARRA:v2p117/r9.anchor: وقوله: اقرأ كتابك [14] : فيها- والله أعلم- (يقال) مضمرة.

FARRA:v2p119/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p119/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p119/r7.claim: In كفى بنفسك and similar phrases, bāʾ may be removed and the noun raised; bāʾ is allowed in praise or blame, not ordinary verbs such as قام or قعد.
FARRA:v2p119/r7.anchor: فلو ألقيت الباء كان الحرف مرفوعا

FARRA:v2p119/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p119/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p119/r8.claim: Poetry supports the construction كفى الهدي, with the noun raised after كفى.
FARRA:v2p119/r8.anchor: كفى الهدي عما غيب المرء مخبرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r6.claim: The command to read may intensify reproach and rebuke through the person's reading of the record.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r6.anchor: لما في قراءته من زيادة التقريع والتوبيخ

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r7.claim: Alternatively, reading makes the person acknowledge his own deeds against himself.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r8.claim: حسيبا may mean that the person is a witness against himself.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r9.claim: Alternatively, حسيبا means that the person judges his own deeds, good or bad.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r9.anchor: الثاني : يعني حاكما بعملك من خير أو شر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r10.claim: God has dealt fairly by making each person account for himself through his own deeds.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r10.anchor: ولقد أنصفك من جعلك حسيبا على نفسك بعملك

MUQATIL:17:13-14/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:13-14/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:13-14/r2.claim: The person is told to read the book; 'enough is yourself as reckoner' means a witness better than oneself cannot be found.
MUQATIL:17:13-14/r2.anchor:
يعني شهيدا، فلا شاهد عليك أفضل من نفسك، وذلك حين قالوا:
والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين
[الأنعام: 23]

MUQATIL:17:13-14/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:13-14/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:13-14/r3.claim: When people claim they were not polytheists in 6:23, God seals their tongues and makes their limbs testify to associationism and denial; this illustrates the verse's self-witnessing.
MUQATIL:17:13-14/r3.anchor:
والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين
[الأنعام: 23]، ختم الله على ألسنتهم، ثم أمر الجوارح، فشهدت عليه بشركه وتكذيبه

MUQATIL:17:13-14/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:13-14/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:13-14/r4.claim: The parallel in 75:14 means a person's own limbs testify against them, including the self, tongue, hands, and feet.
MUQATIL:17:13-14/r4.anchor:
بل الإنسان على نفسه بصيرة
[القيامة: 14]، يعني جوارحهم حين شهدت عليهم أنفسهم، وألسنتهم، وأيديهم، وأرجلهم.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p253/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p253/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p253/r1.claim: Ḥasīban means sufficient, or one who reckons and calls to account.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p253/r1.anchor: {كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا} أي كافيا. ويقال: حاسبا ومحاسبا.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r4.claim: The narration continues that God will say to the person to read the book.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r4.anchor: حال من يلقاه يعنى غير مطوى ليمكنه قراءته

NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r1.claim: The book is the record of one's deeds, and every person is resurrected able to read.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r1.anchor: أي كتاب أعمالك وكل يبعث قارئا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r2.claim: The bāʾ in “by yourself” is extra, so the phrase means that the self suffices as judge.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r3.claim: Ḥasīban is an accusative of specification and means an accountant; ʿalayka attaches to it in the construction “he reckoned this against him.”
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r3.anchor: تمييز وهو بمعنى حاسب وعلى متعلق به

NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, ḥasīban means sufficient, taking the place of a witness, because a witness suffices the claimant regarding what concerns him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r4.anchor: أو بمعنى الكافى وضع موضع الشهيد فعدى بعلى لأن الشاهد يكفى المدعى ما أهمه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r5.claim: The word ḥasīban is masculine because witness, judge, and official roles usually belonged to men; the soul is treated as a man or understood as the person.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281#2/r5.anchor: وإنما ذكر حسيبا لأنه بمنزلة الشهيد والقاضي والأمير إذ الغالب أن يتولى هذه الأمور الرجال

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r16.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r16.claim: Hasan says everyone reads their book, whether literate or not.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r16.anchor: قال الحسن: يقرأ الإنسان كتابه أميا كان أو غير أميا.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r17.claim: Ḥasīb means one who reckons or holds to account; a pious saying pictures the tongue as pen, saliva as ink, and limbs as the page and witnesses.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r17.anchor: أي محاسبا. وقال بعض الصلحاء: هذا كتاب، لسانك قلمه، وريقك مداده

RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r1.claim: The passage follows the completed explanation of signs and warning: because revelation has removed excuses, each person will face a record and answer for deeds.
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r1.anchor: كل ما يحتاج إليه من دلائل التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد فقد صار مذكورا

RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r2.claim: A second link is that God’s provision of worldly and religious benefits entails that people should serve and obey Him, so their deeds are questioned.
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r2.anchor: وذلك يقتضي وجوب اشتغالهم بخدمته وطاعته

RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r3.claim: A third link is that creation is for worship; the sun, moon, night, and day enable obedience, which is then assessed at resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r3.anchor: فلما شرح أحوال الشمس والقمر والليل والنهار

RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r5.claim: An unstated speaker—God through the angels—tells the person to read the book.
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r5.anchor: وهذا القائل هو الله تعالى على ألسنة الملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r6.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r6.claim: Hasan says the person reads the record whether literate or illiterate.
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r6.anchor: يقرؤه أميا كان أو غير أمي

RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r7.speaker: بكر بن عبد الله
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r7.claim: Bakr ibn Abd Allah describes a believer reading good deeds displayed on the record’s back and sins inside, then receiving private forgiveness and great joy.
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r7.anchor: يؤتى بالمؤمن يوم القيامة بصحيفته وهو يقرؤها وحسناته في ظهرها

RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r8.claim: “Accountant” means the person himself will reckon and audit his deeds.

RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r9.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r9.claim: Hasan calls it just that God makes each person their own accountant.
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r9.anchor: عدل والله في حقك من جعلك حسيب نفسك

RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r10.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r10.claim: Al-Suddi says the disbeliever asks to judge himself in light of God’s declaration that He is not unjust to servants.
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r10.anchor: يقول الكافر يومئذ إنك قضيت أنك لست بظلام للعبيد

RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r3.claim: Repeated voluntary acts form stable habits in the soul; each act leaves an effect, as repeated water drops eventually bore a stone.
RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r3.anchor: تكرار الأعمال الاختيارية تفيد حدوث الملكة النفسانية الراسخة في جوهر النفس

RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r4.claim: Because conventional letters merely signify sounds by human agreement while soul-impressions are essential and lasting, the latter better deserve the name “book.”
RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r4.anchor: دلالة تلك النقوش على تلك المعاني المخصوصة دلالة كائنة جوهرية واجبة الثبوت

RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r1.claim: Every deed leaves a trace in the soul: attraction from creation toward God brings felicity, while attraction away from God toward created things brings misery.
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r1.anchor: كل عمل يصدر من الإنسان كثيرا كان أو قليلا قويا كان أو ضعيفا

RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r2.claim: The body’s governance hides these traces; when its bond ends at death, the soul rises and the Resurrection begins in this spiritual sense.

RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r3.claim: The opened book is the soul’s previously hidden worldly impressions, now exposed after bodily attachment ends and read by the intellect.
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r3.anchor: ونخرج له عند حصول هذه القيامة من عمق البدن المظلم كتابا مشتملا على جميع تلك الآثار

RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r4.claim: On this spiritual interpretation, the person’s own soul-impressions reveal whether their effects entail felicity or misery.
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r4.anchor: فإن تلك الآثار إن كانت من موجبات السعادة حصلت السعادة لا محالة

RAZI-FULL:v20p137/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p137/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p137/r1.claim: Razi affirms the apparent narrated events as true while allowing the spiritual interpretations; he calls affirming both the sound, straight approach.
RAZI-FULL:v20p137/r1.anchor: الأحوال الظاهرة التي وردت فيها الروايات حق وصدق لا مرية فيها

NAHHAS:v2p419/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p419/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p419/r1.claim: The imperative اقرأ is marked by dropping the hamza’s ḍamma; Arabs also replace hamza, and Zuhayr’s verse is cited.
NAHHAS:v2p419/r1.anchor: علامة الجزم والبناء حذف الضمة من الهمزة ، وحكي عن العرب : أقر يا هذا ، على إبدال الهمزة ، ومنه وقول زهير

NAHHAS:v2p419/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p419/r2.speaker: زهير
NAHHAS:v2p419/r2.claim: Zuhayr’s cited line is وإلا يبد بالظلم يظلم; it witnesses the reported pronunciation in the discussion of hamza replacement.
NAHHAS:v2p419/r2.anchor: على إبدال الهمزة ، ومنه وقول زهير

NAHHAS:v2p419/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p419/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p419/r3.claim: In كفى بنفسك, the noun is nominative and bāʾ is added for emphasis; حسيبا is either specification or circumstantial.
NAHHAS:v2p419/r3.anchor: ^ ( كفى بنفسك ) ^ في موضع رفع والباء زائدة للتوكيد . ^ ( حسيبا ) ^ على البيان ، وإن شئت على الحال

NAHHAS:v2p419/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p419/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p419/r4.claim: Abu Ishaq allows the non-Qurʾanic feminine form حسيبة.
NAHHAS:v2p419/r4.anchor: قال أبو اسحاق : ويجوز في غير القرآن حسيبة

STUDYQURAN:17:13/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r6.claim: The open book is the record of one’s deeds, familiar to the person and God; hidden earthly deeds and consequences become manifest in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r6.anchor: That an individual’s book is wide open indicates that its contents are well known to the individual as well as to God

STUDYQURAN:17:13/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r7.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r7.claim: Many commentators say two angels assigned to each person record good and evil deeds.
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r7.anchor: The recording of deeds is often ascribed to two angels assigned to every individual, one recording good deeds and the other evil deeds

STUDYQURAN:17:13/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r8.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī metaphorically pictures each deed as a drop leaving an impression on the soul’s rock; repeated habits help inscribe a person’s destiny.
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r8.anchor: Al-Rāzī, however, describes the spiritual reality of this recording metaphorically, suggesting that every deed one commits in life is like a drop of water

STUDYQURAN:17:13/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r9.claim: God, perhaps speaking through angels, commands each person to read the record and thereby judge whether their own deeds merit Garden or Fire.
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r9.anchor: who issues the command in v. 14, Read your book!

STUDYQURAN:17:13/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r10.claim: Although divine mercy remains beyond calculation and inspires hope, people are saved or condemned through their actions; God does not wrong them, they wrong themselves.
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r10.anchor: human beings are saved or condemned through their own actions. For this reason, the Quran repeatedly states that God does not wrong people

STUDYQURAN:17:13/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r11.claim: The book can be one’s soul inscribed with deeds, and the Quran elsewhere depicts one’s limbs testifying against one at Judgment.
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r11.anchor: the Quran offers elsewhere the powerful image of one’s own limbs testifying against one on the Day of Judgment

STUDYQURAN:17:13/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r12.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r12.claim: Some describe the book as the person themself, with tongue as pen, saliva as ink, limbs as paper, and memory as the dictated record.
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r12.anchor: Your tongue is its pen, your saliva is its ink, and your limbs are the paper upon which it is written

TAB-FULL:v14p525/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p525/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p525/r1.claim: The command to read follows an omitted phrase, meaning God will tell each person to read the register of deeds kept and counted by the recording angels.
TAB-FULL:v14p525/r1.anchor: [الإسراء: 14] اقرأ كتاب عملك الذي عملته في الدنيا، الذي كان كاتبانا يكتبانه،

TAB-FULL:v14p525/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p525/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p525/r2.claim: The person is sufficient as their own accountant: no outside witness or other recorder is needed to enumerate the person's deeds.
TAB-FULL:v14p525/r2.anchor: لا نبتغي عليك شاهدا غيرها، ولا نطلب عليك محصيا سواها

TAB-FULL:v14p525/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p525/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p525/r3.claim: Qatāda says that on that day even those who could not read in worldly life will read their record.
TAB-FULL:v14p525/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا} [الإسراء: 14] سيقرأ يومئذ من لم يكن قارئا في الدنيا

TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r1.claim: The displayed book is each person's own record and contains every deed without omission.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r1.anchor: أن الكتاب الذي يخرج له هو كتابه نفسه لا يتعلق بغيره

TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r2.claim: The record shows deeds in their true realities, with their good or evil results exposed beyond concealment or excuse.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r2.anchor: وثالثا أن الأعمال التي أحصاها بادية فيها بحقائقها من سعادة أو شقاء

TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r3.claim: The record contains the actual deeds themselves, made visible to the person, rather than written symbols like ordinary books.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r3.anchor: أن الكتاب يتضمن نفس الأعمال بحقائقها دون الرسوم المخطوطة على حد الكتب المعمولة فيما بيننا

TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r4.claim: The bird and book refer to the same deed; calling it a book at resurrection avoids suggesting it only then becomes a book or was previously hidden despite clinging to its owner.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r4.anchor: أن المراد بالطائر والكتاب في الآية أمر واحد وهو العمل الذي يعمله الإنسان

TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r5.claim: God brings the book out from behind heedlessness on Judgment Day and makes its details visible, already prepared for its owner.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r5.anchor: كتاب الأعمال بحقائقها مستور عن إدراك الإنسان محجوب وراء حجاب الغفلة

TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r6.claim: The book confirms that a person will inevitably meet the consequences of his deeds, since they both cling to him and will be openly displayed.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r6.anchor: الإنسان ستناله تبعة عمله لا محالة أما أولا فلأنه لازم له لا يفارقه

TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r7.claim: In the phrase كفى بنفسك, the bāʾ is emphatic and زائد; the feminine verb may take masculine agreement because its subject is grammatically feminine but not natural feminine.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r7.anchor: الباء فيه زائدة للتأكيد وأصله كفت نفسك وإنما لم يؤنث الفعل

TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r8.claim: An alternative grammatical analysis treats كفى as an indeclinable verb meaning اكتف and the bāʾ as non زائد.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r8.anchor: وربما قيل إنه اسم فعل بمعنى اكتف والباء غير زائدة

TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r9.claim: The record is conclusive evidence even against the sinner who reads it, because he directly witnesses the deed and its recompense.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r9.anchor: حجة للكتاب قاطعة بحيث لا يرتاب فيها قارئه ولو كان هو المجرم نفسه

TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r1.claim: The surrounding rebuke links human haste to the record of deeds: people fail to distinguish benefit from harm and rush after desires, though every deed remains with its doer and will be reviewed.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r1.anchor: أنزل القرآن وجعله هاديا إلى ملة هي أقوم جريا على السنة الإلهية في هداية الناس

TABATABAI:17:22#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:22#2/r8.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:17:22#2/r8.claim: Khalid ibn Yahya reports that the servant recalls every deed and its record as if doing it at that moment, explaining the complaint that nothing small or large is omitted.
TABATABAI:17:22#2/r8.anchor: عن خالد بن يحيى عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

TABRISI:17:13/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:13/r5.claim: Nafsika is the subject of kafa and hasiban is accusative as specification; al-Sarraj instead posits an omitted subject and parses hasiban as circumstantial.
TABRISI:17:13/r5.anchor: موضع بنفسك رفع لأنه فاعل كفى وحسيبا نصب على التمييز له

TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r5.claim: The imperative is elliptical for 'it will be said to him: read your book'; Qatada says even the previously illiterate will read.
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r5.anchor: ها هنا حذف أي ويقال له اقرأ كتابك قال قتادة يقرأ يومئذ

TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r6.claim: A person will recall all recorded deeds as if doing them at that moment, explaining the comparison with the record in al-Kahf.
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r6.anchor: وروى جابر بن خالد بن نجيح عن أبي عبد الله ع قال: يذكر العبد جميع أعماله

TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r7.claim: Seeing every deed and its just recompense leaves no defense and shows the gathered people that God wrongs no one; al-Hasan praises this fairness.
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r7.anchor: قال الحسن يا ابن آدم لقد أنصفك من جعلك حسيب نفسك

THALABI:v6p89/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p89/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p89/r4.claim: The person is told to read his book; he himself suffices as his reckoner and requiter.
THALABI:v6p89/r4.anchor: اقرأ كتابك يعني فيقال له اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم

THALABI:v6p89/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p89/r5.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p89/r5.claim: On that day even a person who did not act as his own reckoner in worldly life will read his record.
THALABI:v6p89/r5.anchor: قتادة: سيقرأ يومئذ كل من لم يكن في الدنيا

THALABI:v6p89/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p89/r6.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v6p89/r6.claim: God has acted justly by making each person his own reckoner.
THALABI:v6p89/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: [قد عدل والله عليك] من جعلك حسيب نفسك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r1.speaker: الفراء والكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī supply an omitted yaqulu, 'it is said/read,' comparing 40:46 and 3:106.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r2.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says everyone will read the record, whether literate or illiterate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r2.anchor: قال الحسن يقرأه أميا كان (¬3) أو غير أمي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r3.claim: Qatāda says even someone who could not read in life will read on that day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: سيقرأ يومئذ من لم يكن قارئا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r4.speaker: بكر بن عبد الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r4.claim: A believer's good deeds appear on the outside of the record and are envied; after fearing his inner list of sins is ruinous, he is told they were forgiven and recites 69:19.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r4.anchor: يؤتى المؤمن يوم القيامة صحيفة حسناته في ظهره يغبطه الناس عليها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r5.claim: Ḥasīb means accountant, as in the related description of God in 33:39.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r6.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan calls it God's justice that He makes a person account for himself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r6.anchor: قال الحسن: عدل والله عليك، من جعلك حسيب نفسك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r7.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r7.claim: Al-Suddī says the unbeliever asks to audit himself because God declared He is not unjust to servants, then is told to read his book.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p281/r7.anchor: وقال السدي: يقول الكافر يومئذ: إنك قضيت أنك لست بظلام للعبيد

SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r1.claim: اقرأ is introduced by an omitted saying verb, and its clause is either an adjective or a circumstantial phrase like the preceding clause.
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r1.anchor: اقرأ }: على إضمار القول، أي: يقال له: اقرأ

SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r2.claim: The common analysis makes كفى a past verb with the noun governed by extra باء as its subject; poetry shows the subject can surface without باء.
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r2.anchor: المشهور عند المعربين: أن " كفى " فعل ماض، والفاعل هو المجرور بالباء

SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r3.claim: The feminine subject might predict feminine agreement, as in Quranic examples, but masculine agreement is allowed because the gender is figurative.
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r3.anchor: كقوله: مآ آمنت قبلهم من قرية

SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r4.claim: A second analysis makes the addressee the subject and كفى an imperative meaning suffice yourself; the author finds it weak because it accepts verbal inflections.
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r4.anchor: والثاني: أن الفاعل/ ضمير المخاطب، و " كفى " على هذا اسم فعل أمر

SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r5.claim: A third analysis supplies an implicit subject meaning sufficiency, a construction said to have been discussed earlier.
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r5.anchor: الثالث: أن فاعل " كفى " ضمير يعود على الاكتفاء

SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r6.anchor: وقد تقدم الكلام على هذا مستوفى. و " اليوم " نصب ب " كفى "

SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses حسيبا as specification meaning one who reckons, and relates عليه through حسب عليه; the examples are cited from Sibawayh.
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r7.anchor: كضريب القداح بمعنى ضاربها، وصريم بمعنى صارم، ذكرهما سيبويه

SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r8.claim: He also allows حسيبا to mean sufficient, standing for witness; عليه then marks what the witness suffices the claimant about.
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى الكافي ووضع موضع الشهيد، فعدي ب " على "

SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r9.claim: He explains the masculine حسيبا by likening the self to a man serving as witness, judge, or trustee, and allows نفس to mean person, supported by a poem.
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r9.anchor: لأنه بمنزلة الشاهد والقاضي والأمين، وهذه الأمور يتولاها الرجال

SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r10.claim: حسيبا may instead be circumstantial; another gloss takes it as محاسب, one who calls someone to account, like خليط and جليس.
SAMIN-DURR:17:14/r10.anchor: والثاني: أنه منصوب على الحال، وذكر لما تقدم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:12-14/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:12-14/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:12-14/r7.claim: The person is told to read his own book and suffices to account for himself that day.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:12-14/r7.anchor: { اقرأ كتابك } أي يقال له: اقرأ كتابك { كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا } محاسبا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r8.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r8.claim: Qatāda says even those who could not read in worldly life will read their record at the Resurrection.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r8.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، قال: سيقرأ يومئذ من لم يكن قارئا في الدنيا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r9.speaker: أبي بن كعب
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r9.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reports that people are summoned for judgment; one who led many people toward good is called by name and given a record with sins inside and good deeds on its back.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r9.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، قال: يدعى الخلائق يوم القيامة للحساب، فإذا كان الرجل في الخير رأسا يدعو إليه،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r10.speaker: أبي بن كعب
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r10.claim: In Ubayy’s account, the person first fears the sins, then finds them forgiven; his good deeds are doubled, his face brightens, he is adorned and given the book in his right hand.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r10.anchor: فيبدأ بالسيئات فيقرأها فيشفق ويتغير لونه، فإذا بلغ آخر الكتاب وجد فيه: هذه سيئاتك وقد غفرت لك

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r11.speaker: أبي بن كعب
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r11.claim: The honored person is given a crown, two garments, ornaments at every joint, and a stature of sixty cubits, identified as Adam’s height.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r11.anchor: ويؤتى بتاج فيوضع على رأسه، ويكسى حلتين، ويحلى كل مفصل منه، ويطول ستين ذراعا، وهي قامة آدم،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r12.speaker: أبي بن كعب
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r12.claim: He is told to go announce the same reward to his companions, quotes 69:19–23, and explains that God’s honor changed his appearance when they ask who he is.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r12.anchor: فيقال له: انطلق إلى أصحابك فبشرهم وأخبرهم أن لكل إنسان منهم مثل هذا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p122#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p122#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p122#2/r1.claim: Being one’s own reckoner means being one’s own witness.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p122#2/r1.anchor: قوله: {كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا} [الإسراء: 14] شاهدا.

ELMALILI:17:13-14/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:13-14/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:13-14/r2.claim: At resurrection each person receives an opened record of deeds and account and is told to read it; the self is sufficient as its own accountant.
ELMALILI:17:13-14/r2.anchor: bir kitap -a‘mâlini kayd ve hesâbını irâe eden bir defter- çıkaracağız

ELMALILI:17:13-14/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:13-14/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:13-14/r3.claim: Elmalılı exhorts people to examine themselves daily and take their own account before they are called to account.
ELMALILI:17:13-14/r3.anchor: insan dünyada da her gün kendini okumalı, hesâba çekilmezden evvel kendini muhasebeye çekmeli

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r3.claim: Each person is bound by their own actions and will see the result when the record of deeds is opened.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r3.anchor: her insan yaptığı ile kendini bağlamış, sorumluluk altına girmiştir, sonucunu da önüne amel defteri konularak görecektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r4.claim: After the discussion of revelation, faith, reward, and punishment, there is no excuse: each person bears responsibility and is told to read their own record and judge themselves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r4.anchor: Bütün bunlardan sonra 13. âyette artık insanlar için mazeret kalmadığı belirtilmek üzere, mahşer meydanında toplanan herkesin sorumluluğunun kendi omuzunda olacağı

ZAJJAJ:v3p231/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p231/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p231/r1.claim: بنفسك is nominative in syntactic position despite the prefixed ب; the sense is that one's own self suffices as a witness against oneself.
ZAJJAJ:v3p231/r1.anchor: (بنفسك) في موضع رفع، وإن كان مجرورا بالباء

ZAJJAJ:v3p231/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p231/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p231/r2.claim: Outside the Quran, حسيبة could be used; the meaning is that the self has sufficed as its own reckoner.
ZAJJAJ:v3p231/r2.anchor: جاز. . كفى بنفسك اليوم حسيبة، والمعنى كفت نفسك حسيبة

ZAJJAJ:v3p231/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p231/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p231/r3.claim: حسيبا is accusative as a specification (تمييز).

ASAD-NOTES:17:13#n18/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:13#n18/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:17:13#n18/r1.claim: The record and account allegorize a person's full comprehension of their past life on Judgment Day; related images appear in 37:19, 39:68, and 50:22.
ASAD-NOTES:17:13#n18/r1.anchor: represent man's total comprehension, on Judgment Day, of all his past life (Razi). This allegory occurs in the Qur'an in many formulations

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p89/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p89/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p89/r3.claim: The doubled verb laqqā is transitive to two objects; passivization makes one the subject and leaves the other as object.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p89/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p89/r4.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p89/r4.claim: Hamza and al-Kisāʾī’s imāla on qāf is acceptable, as is leaving the vowel unchanged.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p89/r4.anchor: وإمالة حمزة والكسائي القاف حسنة وتركها حسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r10.claim: اقرأ كتابك is governed by an implied “it is said to him”; Qatāda says even those unable to read will read that day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r10.anchor: اقرأ كتابك معمول لقول محذوف أي يقال له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and others make بنفسك the subject of كفى, with bāʾ extra; Abū Ḥayyān says it may be omitted without necessity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r1.anchor: وقال الزمخشري وغيره. وبنفسك فاعل كفى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r2.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r2.claim: Two poems illustrate كفى without bāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r2.anchor: قال الشاعر: كفى الشيب والإسلام للمرء ناهيا وقال آخر: ويخبرني عن غائب المرء هديه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r3.claim: Other parses make the subject a pronoun meaning sufficiency or treat كفى as an imperative-like particle; these do not treat bāʾ as extra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r3.anchor: وقيل: فاعل كفى ضمير يعود على الاكتفاء، أي كفى هو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r4.claim: The apparent بنفسك means “you yourself”; Muqātil says one’s limbs testify if one denies, while Abū ʿUbayda emphasizes what one knows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بنفسك ذاتك أي كفى بك. وقال مقاتل: يريد بنفسه جوارحه تشهد عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r5.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses حسيبا as a judge over deeds and says God made each person their own auditor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r5.anchor: ومعنى حسيبا حاكما عليك بعملك قاله الحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r6.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r6.claim: Al-Kalbī glosses it as accountant; another view takes it as a reckoner or intensive form like judge and ruler.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r6.anchor: وقال الكلبي: محاسبا يعني فعيلا بمعنى مفاعل كجليس وخليط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r7.speaker: الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r7.claim: Al-Anbārī explains masculine حسيبا for feminine نفس because it means the person or lacks a visible feminine marker.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p22/r7.anchor: وقال الأنباري: وإنما قال حسيبا والنفس مؤنثة لأنه يعني بالنفس الشخص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p23/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p23/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p23/r7.claim: A line describing أرض with masculine أبقل supports the grammatical form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p23/r7.anchor: ولا أرض أبقل إبقالها من اهتدى

BURHAN:v1p223/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p223/r1.speaker: أبو بكر القاضي
BURHAN:v1p223/r1.claim: On whether the codex includes all seven revealed modes or one, Abu Bakr al-Qadi favors all; al-Tabari and most later scholars favor one, while al-Shatibi distinguishes the Abu Bakr and Uthman compilations.
BURHAN:v1p223/r1.anchor: وهذا المجموع فى المصحف هل هو جميع الأحرف السبعة التى أقيمت القراءة عليها أو حرف واحد منها ميل القاضى أبى بكر إلى أنه جميعها

BURHAN:v1p223/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p223/r2.speaker: أبو بكر القاضي
BURHAN:v1p223/r2.claim: Al-Qadi says the seven modes were transmitted from the Prophet and recorded by Uthman and the Companions, omitting what lacked mutawatir transmission; their differences are noncontradictory.
BURHAN:v1p223/r2.anchor: وقال الصحيح أن هذه الأحرف السبعة ظهرت واستفاضت عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وضبطها عنه الأئمة وأثبتها عثمان والصحابة فى المصحف

BURHAN:v1p223/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p223/r3.speaker: الطحاوي
BURHAN:v1p223/r3.claim: Al-Tahawi says the seven modes temporarily eased recitation for speakers of different languages; the need later ended and recitation returned to one mode.
BURHAN:v1p223/r3.anchor: والثامن قول الطحاوى أن ذلك كان فى وقت خاص لضرورة دعت إليه لأن كل ذى لغة كان يشق عليه أن يتحول عن لغته

BURHAN:v1p223/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p223/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p223/r4.claim: A ninth explanation takes the modes as types of Quranic knowledge: creation, unity, transcendence, attributes, commands, mercy and punishment, resurrection and accounting, and prophethood.
BURHAN:v1p223/r4.anchor: والتاسع أن المراد علم القرآن يشتمل على سبعة أشياء علم الإثبات والإيجاد

BURHAN:v1p223/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p223/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p223/r5.claim: The accounting mode is illustrated by the command to read one’s record and each person sufficing as his own reckoner.

BURHAN:v4p253/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p253/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p253/r4.claim: The ب in بنفسك is not extra: if it were, the verb would show feminine agreement because نفس is usually feminine.
BURHAN:v4p253/r4.anchor: وأما قوله ﴿ كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا ﴾ فليست زائدة وإلا للحق الفعل قبلها علامة التأنيث لأنه للنفس

BURHAN:v4p253/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p253/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p253/r5.claim: One parsing supplies كان after كفى, with بنفسك as its predicate standing in its place.
BURHAN:v4p253/r5.anchor: وجوز في الفعل وجهان أحدهما أن تكون كان مقدرة بعد كفى ويكون بنفسك صفة له قائمة مقامه

BURHAN:v4p253/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p253/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p253/r6.claim: The other parsing supplies a pronoun explained by the accusative حسيبا, as in نعم رجلا زيد.
BURHAN:v4p253/r6.anchor: والثاني أنه مضمر يفسره المنصوب بعده أعنى حسيبا كقولك نعم رجلا زيد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p72/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p72/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p72/r1.claim: The passage singles out خسأت as the word under examination in the Bedouin couplet.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p72/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p72/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p72/r2.claim: The dawn is said to ‘give permission’ to see because daylight makes sight possible after night had prevented it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p72/r2.anchor: لما كان تعذر الإبصار منعا من الليل ، جعل إمكانه عند ظهور الصبح إذنا من الصبح

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p72/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p72/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p72/r3.claim: Jurjani calls the couplet quoted by al-Jāḥiẓ exceptionally beautiful and points to Bashshār’s related image of carrying a burdensome companion like a boil beneath a skin patch.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p72/r3.anchor: ومما هو في غاية الحسن ، وهو من الفن الأول قول الشاعر ؛ أنشده الجاحظ

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p72/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p72/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p72/r4.claim: The metaphor ‘bridge’ has unequal force across its uses: it is more beautiful for toil as a bridge to comfort than in the first example, with a further use by Rabīʿa al-Raqqī.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p72/r4.anchor: فترى لها في الثاني حسنا لا تراه في الأول . ثم تنظر إليها في قول ربيعة الرقي

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p103/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p103/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p103/r1.claim: Beginning an interrogative with the verb directs denial toward the action itself: its occurrence may be denied, or the action may be presented as improper.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p103/r1.anchor: جملة الأمر أنك تنحو بالإنكار نحو الفعل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p103/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p103/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p103/r2.claim: A verb-first question can challenge an impossible boast or condemn a proposed action; ‘Shall we compel you when you dislike it?’ exemplifies the latter.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p103/r2.anchor: وعلى ذلك قوله تعالى : ( ﴿ أنلزمكموها وأنتم لها كارهون ﴾ )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p103/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p103/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p103/r3.claim: Beginning with the noun instead directs denial toward the person as someone capable or disposed to perform the act, rather than denying the act itself.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p103/r3.anchor: فإن بدأت بالاسم فقلت : أأنت تفعل ؟ أو قلت : أهو يفعل ؟

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r1.claim: Starting with the noun directs denial at the identity or status of the alleged actor, rather than at the action itself.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r1.anchor: وجملة الأمر أن تقديم الاسم يقتضي أنك عمدت بالإنكار إلى ذات من قيل إنه يفعل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r2.claim: ‘Would he kill me while the sword is beside me?’ cannot mean he is incapable of killing: the sword is cited as a means that prevents his action, so the question presumes he could act.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r2.anchor: فذكر ما يكون منعا من الفعل . ومحال أن يقول هو ممن لا يجيء منه الفعل ثم يقول : إني أمنعه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r3.claim: The real force of such interrogatives is to make the hearer reconsider, feel ashamed, desist, or be unable to answer; ‘denial’ is only a label for that effect.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r3.anchor: الذي هو محض المعنى أنه لتنبيه السامع حتى يرجع إلى نفسه ، فيخجل ويرتدع

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r4.claim: Questions about impossible acts are figurative rebukes: they compare a person's boast or hope to an absurd impossibility, rather than assert that anyone expects it literally.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p104/r4.anchor: لا يقرر بالمحال ، وبما لا يقول أحد : إنه يكون إلا على سبيل التمثيل

DAMGHANI:v1p128/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p128/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p128/r5.claim: Ḥasīban can mean a witness: the person’s own self suffices as witness against him.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p184/r3.claim: نستنسخ can mean copy, as يستسخر means mock, or solicit a record by ordering angels to write and preserve deeds; the cited verses show deeds are recorded and counted.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p184/r3.anchor: فقوله: (نستنسخ) يجوز أن يكون ننسخ كقوله: وإذا رأوا آية يستسخرون
